name: Andre Koo Sr
forbes_bio: Koo is the honorary chairman of Chailease Holding, an equipment-leasing outfit operating in Taiwan, mainland China and Southeast Asia.
Chailease comprises over 70 companies with 10,000 employees. It operates in Taiwan, mainland China and 12 other countries and regions.
The first generation of Koos made their fortune in camphor, salt, sugar, and land. Koo's father,  financier Jeffrey Koo, Sr., who died in 2012, was dubbed the "Father of the Credit Card" in Taiwan.
Andre's business empire operates independently from the Koo family's holdings.
Andre, his father and Andre Jr. are all graduates of NYU's Stern School of Business; younger son Mattrew is studying there as an undergraduate. Andre now chairs the board of overseers at NYU Stern.
forbes_facts: The Andre Koo Lobby at NYU's Stern School of Business is named after Koo. He has been sponsoring the school's Andre Koo Tech MBA program since its inception in 2018.
Koo calls himself a true connoisseur of both wine and business jets.

name: Stephen Jarislowsky
name_chinese: 斯蒂芬·贾里斯洛夫斯基
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Stephen Jarislowsky made the bulk of his fortune at the helm of Jarislowsky Fraser, the investment management firm he founded in 1955.
He stepped down as CEO in 2012 but remains chairman emeritus of the company and president of the Jarislowsky Foundation.
Canadian bank Scotiabank bought Jarislowsky Fraser for about $750 million in stock and cash in April 2018.
He owns a sizable art collection that is largely comprised of Canadian art, but also includes Chinese jade and French impressionism.
forbes_facts: Jarislowsky owns the 2,000-acre Marina Island in the Strait of Georgia near Vancouver.
A longtime supporter of business ethics and shareholder rights, Jarislowsky cofounded the Canadian Coalition for Good Governance in 2002 and is an honorary director.

name: Qiu Guanghe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Qiu Guanghe is chairman and founder of Semir Group, the parent of Zhejiang Semir Garment, which makes and sells apparel.
Semir Garment was founded in 2002, focusing on casual wear and children's clothing and now boasts nearly 8,000 stores across China (including franchises).
Qiu founded the fashion retailing group in 1996 in his hometown of Wenzhou, a trading mecca in Zhejiang Province.
Qiu Jianqiang, Qiu's son, chairs Zhejiang Semir Garment.

name: Yi Rubo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2019-2020); Hurun Global (2015-2023); Hurun China (2014-2022)
forbes_bio: Yi Rubo chairs Zhong Ang Group, whose interests include real estate and decoration.
Zhong Ang was established in 2004.

name: George Joseph
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: George Joseph is the founder of Mercury General, an insurance provider with $5.5 billion in annual revenues.
After raising $2 million in capital, he started Mercury General in 1962 and offered cut-rate deals to safer-than-average drivers.
He owns 35% of the publicly traded insurance firm, which offers automotive, home and fire insurance.
Raised amidst the Great Depression, Joseph was a flight navigator during World War II.
He graduated from Harvard with majors in math and physics in 1949.
forbes_facts: Joseph named the company after the Roman god Mercury, because he wanted the company to be nimble in business ventures.

name: Jupally Rameshwar Rao
forbes_bio: Jupally Rameshwar Rao founded My Home Constructions, a residential and commercial property developer, in 1981.
The privately held My Home is a prominent real estate player in the southern Indian city of Hyderabad.
The company's projects span the gamut from apartments to villa communities to office buildings.
The My Home Group also has interests in cement and education.
forbes_facts: Rao was reportedly among the donors for the construction of the 216-foot tall Statue of Equality depicting Ramanuja, an 11th century Hindu philosopher, in Hyderabad.

name: John de Mol
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Dutch entertainment mogul John de Mol is one of the biggest names in reality TV.
With Joop van den Ende, he founded Endemol, the company responsible for international hits "Deal or No Deal," "Fear Factor" and "Big Brother."
De Mol sold Endemol for $5.3 billion to Spanish telecom giant Telefonica in 2000.
In 2015, he sold most of his Talpa Media, creator of hit shows like "The Voice," to British ITV for an initial cash payment of $545 million.
forbes_facts: Endemol is the world's largest independent producer, with more than 800 productions in 76 territories airing on 295 channels around the world.
John de Mol's sister, Linda de Mol, is an actress and the host of the Dutch version of "Deal or No Deal".

name: Joseph 'Pitt' Reeves Hyde III
forbes_bio: Joseph 'Pitt' Reeves Hyde founded auto parts giant AutoZone in 1979.
He served as CEO and board chair until 1996, when he stepped down from both roles after being diagnosed with prostate cancer.
He sold most of his Auto­Zone stock back in the 1990s. Had he kept it, he'd be worth over $10 billion as of September 2025.
His charitable foundation, which he runs with his wife Barbara, has given away more than $300 million, nearly all of which has gone to a smorgasbord of local causes in his hometown of Memphis.
Hyde's family office acquired an undisclosed stake in Elon Musk's xAI through a special purpose vehicle in 2025. He and Barbara know Musk's brother Kimbal, who formerly ran a restaurant in the city.
